title: Brain and Brilliance: Mini Review
content: This paper reviews the link between creativity and psychopathology from a neurological perspective, challenging the mad-genius stereotype with scientific, historical, literary, and artistic examples, as well as modern neuroscience. Multiple case studies demonstrate a correlation among mental health, challenges, and creativity. The review also emphasizes the key roles of default mode network connectivity, HPA axis function, neurotransmitter regulation, and other brain mechanisms involved in creative thinking related to psychopathology. Additionally, it discusses cognitive traits such as working memory, divergent thinking, and openness to experience. The paper also considers the influence of early-life experiences, mentorship, cultural norms, and educational opportunities in fostering creativity. While the review mainly focuses on cognitive and emotional factors, it notes that mental illness may be associated with creativity, but suffering is not necessary. A major takeaway is the positive implications for therapy, creativity, and education in both neurotypical and neurodivergent populations. Finally, it advocates shifting away from romanticized narratives of psychological pain and instead emphasizing the interaction of cognition, brain function, and supportive circumstances as the foundation of creativity.
